clue.text: Male pair moved in front of relative next in line?

indicators.note: letters that have been moved are no longer in their original places, so the word is rearranged

blocks.note: the male pronoun
taken as written, to be rearranged
a parent is a close relative

explanation.surface: A couple of men shuffle along a queue to stand ahead of a family member waiting their turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' simply places the rearranged pair before the relative. The question mark flags that 'next in line' is meant in the royal succession sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The heir apparent is the person whose right to inherit a throne or title cannot be displaced, so is first in the order of succession.

clue.text: City Radio enthusiast brought up food

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up means writing it from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a ham is an amateur radio operator
grub is informal for food

explanation.surface: A radio buff from a city vomits their dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' looks like being sick, but in a down light it signals writing the food word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamburg is a large port city in northern Germany.

clue.text: Popular station platform

blocks.note: something in is fashionable or popular
STA is a standard abbreviation for station

explanation.surface: A busy railway station has a platform that everyone uses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a railway platform; the definition means a social media platform.
explanation.definitionFit: Insta is the casual short name for Instagram, the photo-sharing social media platform.

clue.text: Mass at end of road with song and prayer

blocks.note: AVE is the abbreviation for avenue, a road
M is the symbol for mass in physics
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A church service at the end of the street, with hymns and prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass at end of road' puts the mass letter after the road abbreviation; 'Mass' looks religious, fitting the surface, but is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ave Maria, or Hail Mary, is a traditional Catholic prayer to the Virgin Mary.

clue.text: Felines stuck their noses in reportedly

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: to pry is to stick your nose into others' business

explanation.surface: Cats are said to have been nosy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a collective noun: a group of felines.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is the collective term for a group of lions, the big cats.

clue.text: Tough on one being nursed by mum

indicators.note: something nursed is held in the arms, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: RE means on or about, as in a memo
the Roman numeral for one
mum means saying nothing, as in 'keep mum'

explanation.surface: A tough baby being nursed by its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like a mother nursing a baby, but it is the adjective meaning quiet; the numeral goes inside after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient means able to withstand or recover from hardship, which is being tough.

clue.text: Kissing naked head

indicators.note: something naked has had its covering stripped, so the outer letters come off

blocks.note: snogging is British slang for kissing

explanation.surface: Kissing someone's bald head while undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Snogging is British slang for passionate kissing; removing its first and last letters leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noggin is informal, chiefly British, slang for a person's head.

clue.text: Monk caught adult climbing up with short friend

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means going from bottom to top, so the letters read backwards
short means cut off, so the last letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
A is the film certificate for adult
taken as written
china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), a friend

explanation.surface: A monk is caught climbing up something with a short companion.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate rhymes with mate, so in Cockney rhyming slang a friend is your china; its last letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Capuchin is a friar of a Franciscan order, a kind of monk named for the pointed hood.

clue.text: My clue confused educational establishment

indicators.note: confused things are muddled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter admits one of their clues has baffled a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyceum is a school or college, from Aristotle's Lyceum in Athens; in France a lycée is a secondary school.

clue.text: Setter's row about origin of Telegraph puzzles

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so only its first letter is used
about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: from the setter's own viewpoint, something of theirs is 'my'
a row of things in sequence is a series
first letter of Telegraph

explanation.surface: The setter has had an argument over where the newspaper's crosswords come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as an argument, but here it is a line of things in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysteries are things that baffle and need solving, just as puzzles do.

clue.text: Rolled cheese filled with very hot sauce?

indicators.note: something rolled over is turned the other way, so the word reads backwards
a thing filled with something has it inside, so one piece goes in the other

blocks.note: Yarg is a Cornish cheese wrapped in nettle leaves
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A rolled cheese stuffed with a fiery sauce, as at a fancy dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Yarg is a Cornish cheese wrapped in nettles. 'very hot' looks like one phrase, but 'very' is wordplay and 'hot sauce?' is the definition; the question mark admits gravy is not spicy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravy is a meat-juice sauce served hot over a roast, so it is literally a hot sauce.

clue.text: Ignorant Italian article confronts conflict with Spain

blocks.note: una is the Italian feminine indefinite article, 'a'
a war is an armed conflict
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: An oblivious Italian piece of writing faces up to a war involving Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confronts' just places the article in front of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unaware is to lack knowledge of something, which is being ignorant of it.

clue.text: Free time in isle cycling with banker

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so letters are moved from the end of the word round to its start

blocks.note: taken as written
a banker is a river, which has banks; the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Spending your holiday on an island bike ride with a bank employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a crossword favourite for a river, something that has banks; the last two letters of the island word cycle round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is time when you are not working, which is free time.

clue.text: Antiseptic regime oddly stopped by investigators

indicators.note: acting oddly means behaving in an unusual way, so the letters come out in a strange order
something stopped by another has that other plugged into it, so one goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A cleanliness routine is strangely halted by detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' could suggest taking odd letters, but here it rearranges the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: A germicide is a substance that kills germs, which is what an antiseptic does.

clue.text: Extremely hungry bird on river briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: the raven is a large black bird
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A starving bird briefly lands on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, including the one through York.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenous means voraciously hungry, so it is extreme hunger.

clue.text: Raised fine for pub illegally hiding drug

indicators.note: something hiding another keeps it concealed inside, so the word lies within the run of letters
raised in a down clue means lifted from bottom to top, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the end of fine, all of for and pub, and the start of illegally

explanation.surface: A pub gets a larger fine for illegally concealing narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a court report on a landlord, and 'Raised fine' seems a single phrase; in fact 'Raised' tells you to read the concealed letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common painkilling, anti-inflammatory medicine, so a drug in the medical sense.

clue.text: Fancy greeting Mike after end of show?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: last letter of show
hi is an informal greeting
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Fancy saying hello to Mike once the show is over?
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' means the greeting and Mike follow the final letter of show.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim is a sudden fancy or impulse, as in 'take a fancy to'.

clue.text: Recall greed spreading within Irish party

indicators.note: something spreading is moving about out of its original shape, so the letters are rearranged
within means inside, so the rearranged letters go into the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A politician remembers greed taking hold inside an Irish party.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge up is to bring back an old memory with effort, which is to recall it.

clue.text: Rescue silver taken from primitive

indicators.note: taken from means removed out of, so those letters are subtracted from the word

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
savage means primitive or uncivilised

explanation.surface: Saving the silverware stolen by an uncivilised thief.
explanation.definitionFit: To save someone is to rescue them from danger, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Fried morsel from island close to Tasmania

indicators.note: the close of a word is its ending, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: Samos is a Greek island in the Aegean
last letter of Tasmania

explanation.surface: A deep-fried snack from an island near Tasmania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to Tasmania' reads as a location near Australia, but it means the final letter of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a small fried triangular pastry with a savoury filling, a bite-sized morsel.

clue.text: Total expert welcoming Newton's speech

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: utter means total or complete
an ace is an expert
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: A leading scientist introduces Isaac Newton's lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newton's' looks like the physicist, but it is the unit of force abbreviated to one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An utterance is something spoken, a piece of speech.

clue.text: City hosts a German with a passion

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the other pieces go inside

blocks.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
taken as written
GER is an abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A city warmly receives a German visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely, a small English cathedral city, is a crossword favourite for 'city'.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something eagerly is to do it keenly, with enthusiasm and passion.

clue.text: Piercing noise essentially over in workshop

indicators.note: the essence of something is its heart, so only the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: a stud is an item of jewellery worn in a piercing
middle letter of noise
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A shrill noise is basically finished in a workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piercing noise' seems a phrase for a shriek, but 'Piercing' is the jewellery and 'noise' just gives its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is an artist's or craftsman's workroom, a kind of workshop.

clue.text: Lizard egg laid in heath

indicators.note: something laid in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a moor is open uncultivated heathland
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: A lizard's egg has been laid out on the heath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' tempts as O, but it is the louse egg; it sits inside the heath word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor is a large tropical lizard, such as the Komodo dragon.

clue.text: Husband by border being evasive

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
an edging is a decorative border

explanation.surface: A husband standing at the border dodges questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' suggests a hedge, which is fitting, but the piece is a trimmed edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedging means avoiding a straight answer or commitment, which is being evasive.

clue.text: Vocal group initially abandoned god

indicators.note: something initially abandoned has been dropped at its start, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a chorus is a group of singers

explanation.surface: A choir has walked out on their deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Horus is the falcon-headed sky god of ancient Egyptian religion.

clue.text: Greek characters regularly sit on trams

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Greeks habitually ride on trams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek characters' sounds like people, but means letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, so iotas are Greek letters.

clue.text: Safe inlet of sea

blocks.note: first meaning: secure, in good condition
second meaning: a narrow stretch of sea

explanation.surface: A sheltered bay where boats are safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' could be a noun for a strongbox, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both secure and undamaged, and a channel or inlet of the sea.

clue.text: Performer let go before a tree collapsed

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen into a heap, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: to fire someone is to let them go from a job
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A circus act is called off before a tree comes down.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-eater is a street or circus entertainer who appears to swallow flames.

clue.text: Cereal is followed by hard pale pie

blocks.note: corn is a cereal crop
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
pasty means pale and unhealthy-looking

explanation.surface: Breakfast cereal is followed by a solid, pale pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pale' is the adjective pasty, which happens to be spelt like the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish pasty is a folded pastry case filled with meat and vegetables, a traditional hand pie from Cornwall.
